name: Kuttu Pakora
steps: Peel the potatoes and slice into even 2 mm rounds; thicker slices can stay raw after the batter browns. Pat the slices dry. Finely chop the chilli and coriander.
Mix buckwheat flour, cumin, chilli, coriander and rock salt. Whisk in the water gradually to make a smooth batter that coats a spoon thickly but still falls in a ribbon.
Pour the oil into a deep, heavy pan with plenty of headroom and heat to about 170°C. A small drop of batter should rise steadily with bubbles, not sink or darken immediately.
Dip a potato slice into the batter, let the excess drip briefly and lower it carefully into the oil. Add a few more without crowding or letting the slices stick together.

Fry for 4–6 minutes, turning halfway, until the coating is crisp and the bubbles have slowed. Cut open the first pakora: the potato must be completely tender, with no firm raw centre. Reduce the heat slightly if the outside colours too quickly.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain. Bring the oil back to temperature before frying the next batch. Keep water away from the hot oil and serve the pakoras freshly cooked.
tips: The 600 ml oil is the frying medium, not the amount absorbed. Never fill the pan more than halfway with oil.
notes: Four adult portions. Listed time covers preparation and cooking; additional soaking, cooling or resting is stated separately. Fasting customs vary: check every ingredient against your household practice. Jain suitability depends on your saved ingredient rules.
